items.topic: Lam Research (LRCX) Q1 FY2027 results and stock reaction
items.facts: Lam Research reported record quarterly revenue of $8.22B and adjusted EPS of $2.20, both ahead of Street estimates. December-quarter revenue guide of $8.2-9.0B came in below the $8.53B consensus; the CFO said guidance 'would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints.' Lam raised its 2026-2027 wafer-fab-equipment spending forecast, expecting the industry to spend over $200B in 2027. Stock fell ~9-12% depending on the report (this system's own close: -11.76% to $230.15). Applied Materials fell ~6-8% and ASML fell ~4% the same session on the same read-through.
items.caveat: This system's own script-verified close (-11.76%) is used for magnitude; third-party outlets reported a range (-8% to -12%) depending on measurement time. Press cited only for the stated reason, per §4C.

items.topic: Chip-equipment and AI-optical complex selloff, same session
items.facts: The 24/7 Wall St report names Applied Materials and ASML as falling alongside Lam Research on the same guidance/supply-constraint read-through. This system's own scan additionally shows KLA, Teradyne, Coherent, Lumentum, Ciena, Marvell, Micron, Western Digital and SanDisk all down >4-13% the same session (data/raw/movers_2026-10-22.json).
items.caveat: No dated, named-source reporting was found tying KLA, Teradyne, Coherent, Lumentum, Ciena, Marvell, Micron, Western Digital or SanDisk specifically to Lam's guidance or to any distinct news of their own; reported as a sector-wide pattern, not individually attributed causes, per §4C/§5.

items.topic: GE Vernova, Vistra and other AI-power-adjacent decliners
items.facts: GE Vernova (-10.64%), Vistra (-9.80%) and Bloom Energy (-8.70%) all fell the same session (data/raw/movers_2026-10-22.json). GE Vernova's own next earnings report is confirmed for 2026-10-28, so today's move is not an earnings reaction for that name.
items.caveat: No same-day, named-source catalyst found tying these three together; reported as a mechanical pattern only in Tier 3, not asserted as a single causal story, per §4C.

items.facts: No credible same-day market-wrap headline naming a single unifying cause for the day's broad dispersion (160 S&P 500 names moving >4%) was found via web search; the scale is consistent with this week sitting deep in Q3 earnings season (Honeywell and Lam Research both reported this week, among many others) rather than one shared catalyst.
